mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above the 5-year monthly average precedes a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return by reducing real interest rates and boosting risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5-year monthly average in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite FEDFUNDS above average, with no significant change in volatility proxies.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE predicts a 5-day S&P 500 forward return positive as labor market strength offsets inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative when PAYEMS up and UNRATE also up, or correlation <0.3 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST and a concurrent drop in INDPRO together signal excess demand, driving a 60-day S&P 500 forward return positive via supply-chain compression.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns flat or negative despite persistent HOUST/INDPRO pattern, or inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises >2% in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) predicts a 20-day negative S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates weaker earnings and corporate profit compression.
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite continued GDPC1 decline, or GDP growth resumes above -1% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below its 10-month moving average for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a 60-day negative forward return as investors anticipate prolonged tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS below 10-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS below trend, or alternative monetary signals (CPIAUCSL) show cooling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS exceeding the prior 6 months' high coincides with a 5-day positive S&P 500 forward return as strong hiring signals economic resilience.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 6-month high in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day return negative when PAYEMS spikes but other labor indicators (UNRATE) remain unchanged or rise.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both INDPRO and RSAFS predict a 20-day negative S&P 500 forward return as weak industrial production and retail sales indicate contraction.
candidate_trigger: both INDPRO and RSAFS decrease in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite continued declines in both proxies, or alternative demand proxies (HOUST) also fall.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, the S&P 500 shows a 5-day positive forward return as lower borrowing costs boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months and not in recession regime
regime_hint: low-rate environment not coinciding with recession
failure_condition: 5-day return negative despite UNRATE below 4%, or recession is detected in macro indicators (e.g., GDP decline in GDPC1).
